Estimated cost includes allowances for tuition and fees (based on 18 credit hours each academic year in the College of Liberal Arts & Sciences; other programs may have additional course fees), room and board, and books. For financial aid purposes, other estimated costs are $2,748 for transportation and $3,464 for personal expenses.
International students should use International Support Services’ cost calculator to estimate their costs of attendance.
Questions should be directed to the Office of the University Registrar.

Tuition and fees
KU’s tuition rate is reviewed every year by KU leadership and approved by the Kansas Board of Regents. We take tuition seriously and communicate transparently about changes to rates and how student dollars are spent.
In short: Your bill is made up of tuition, campus fees, and, depending on your degree program, course fees. Online graduate tuition is a flat rate per credit hour that varies by program, with no additional required fees. Use the tools below to find the numbers for your program.

Quick answers
Graduate tuition and fees questions, answered
The questions prospective graduate students ask most about who sets tuition, what fees cover, and where to find the numbers for their program.
Expand all
Who sets tuition at KU?
KU leadership reviews the tuition rate every year, and the Kansas Board of Regents approves it. KU communicates transparently about changes to rates and how student dollars are spent. To estimate tuition for your program, use the graduate tuition and fee calculator.
What do KU campus fees pay for?
Campus fees support health and wellness, recreation facilities, campus unions, transit, child care, campus sustainability, and other resources accessible to all KU students. On-campus graduate students pay required fees, while online graduate students have no additional required fees. Use KU’s graduate tuition and fee calculator to see the current amounts.
Will I pay program course fees?
Depending on your degree program, you may also pay course fees that support academic programs and instruction in your school. Course fees are separate from campus fees, and some programs may have additional ones. For details, review KU’s cost tools or ask the Office of the University Registrar.
How much does online graduate tuition cost?
Online graduate tuition is a flat rate per credit hour that varies by program, no matter where you live. There are no additional required fees for online students. Use KU’s graduate tuition and fee calculator to estimate what your program will cost.
What does the estimated annual cost include?
The estimate includes allowances for tuition and fees, room and board, and books. For financial aid purposes, transportation and personal expenses are added as other estimated costs. Your own cost depends on your resident status and degree path, so use the estimated cost of attendance as a guide.
How do international students estimate their costs?
International students should use International Support Services’ estimated cost of attendance to plan their costs. It is the resource designed for international students, so use it alongside the graduate tuition and fee calculator when budgeting for your first year. Your estimate depends on your degree type and area of study.
Where can I ask questions about tuition and fees?
Send questions about tuition and fees to the Office of the University Registrar. For billing questions, contact Student Accounts and Receivables. You can also review KU’s cost tools for calculators and cost tables. To explore graduate funding and aid, visit our Funding and aid page.
